chapter: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers
title: Four and a half years with Art Blakey: ears open, mouth shut
summary: He stayed close to Blakey as an apprenticeship, accepting blunt criticism as a sign of love.

blocks.x: Tell us about playing with one of the absolute masters of jazz, an institution within himself. Tell us about Art Blakey.

Yeah, he was, when I was with him first of all, I was with him four and a half years and so I just hung out with him. I didn’t try to tell him nothing. You know I see a lot of young kids, they don’t know how to keep their mouth shut, you know? That’s the biggest thing you’ve got to learn how to do is keep your ears open and your mouth shut. You know? Ears open, mouth shut. And that’s what I did with Art. And he appreciated that. If Art asked me my opinion on something, I would give it. He’d say “what do you think about © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

this, Bobby?” Well I think this— But I never try to tell him anything of my own personal experiences, because I figured what can I tell him? He’s played with Bird and everybody, and so there was nothing that I was going to tell him, my experiences aren’t relevant to this man. And if he wants to know — the only thing that’s relevant to this man is my performance on the bandstand and for me trying to be the best Jazz Messenger I can be and to make sure that he’s happy. So I took it as an apprenticeship for four years, at least to lay that groundwork. So but with that in mind, I hung out with him anywhere. After the gig I went home with him to his room, I called him first thing in the morning to check in and where you going? You going to eat? I’m going with you. So for four and a half years I was under his armpit. The other guys, you know, they split after the gig. I went with him. Because the thing about Art that would scare a lot of people is that you know that if he loved you, and the more he got to know you, at one point he’s going to bust you. He could read you. He’d look at you and he can read you. He knew your weaknesses and your strengths, on the instrument and in your personality. And being around him, you knew that. I don’t know, it was just a feeling that you knew he was looking right through you. And so that’s scary. Because no one wants to get criticized. But if you’re going to, one of the prices you have to pay to hang out with a man like this, is you’re going to get criticized. At some point he’s going to tell you what he really thinks about you. And what he really thinks about your playing. And you know it. And so a lot of guys would get away. But I stayed up there to the hammer. And every so often he’d tell me “Bob, you’re not swinging” but he wouldn’t say it like that. “Bobby, you’re not swinging. You sound like you’re playing out of an exercise book.” And you know that’s pretty shocking, you know? But he’s telling the truth. And you’d have to think about it. Or he would say “you’re overblowing your horn—you’re out of tune—you’re blowing too hard, just relax.” And those are the things that helped me. Because I took it to heart and I was at the age where I was like open to that. And I didn’t have a block-up in my mind, so he could work with me, like putty in his hands. But at the same time you have to submit yourself to that. So it’s a sense of submission is where you gain your strength. Because if a man loves you and you submit to him, you only got to do it one time. Because you will learn, and then you’ve got that. And then the next time, you’ll have to submit to something else, but if you do that long enough, you’ll cover everything. And you see people who have a lot of resistance in their heart to criticism. And you know that they’re never going to learn and get past a certain point because all the great ones, when you’re being around a person like Art, you realize that’s how they talk to each other. They were brutally honest. Brutally honest. And they always told the truth, the way they saw it. And you had to think about it. Because they really don’t want to say nothing to you. And the only reason they © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
would say something to you is that they loved you. If they didn’t love you they’d say, “Yeah baby, you sound good.” They tell you what you want to hear.
